$comment: Track A perf baseline — the committed, diff-visible copy of every perf claim that can be
stated as an exact integer. Enforced by `bun run check:perf` (counters + published bytes +
the rubber-stamp guard) and `bun run check:perf-freshness` (are the wall-clock numbers still
about this code). Spec: docs/plans/perf-measurement-2026-07.md §4 and §11.5.
`counters` is regenerated with `bun scripts/check-perf.mjs --write`. Do not hand-edit it to
make a red gate green: a counter that moved is a published claim that changed, and changing
it in the same commit as `packages/*/src` requires a dated `reviews` entry.
`bundleBytes.ceiling` is the gzipped tarball size npm pack reports, with ~10% headroom.
`--write --bytes` creates missing ceilings and tightens slack ones; it never RAISES one.
`freshness.suites` lists each bench suite's DIRECT engine imports; the gate expands them
through the workspace dependency graph at run time, so `render` automatically drags in
`math` and nobody has to remember that in review.

reviews.reason: PERF-5: first population. Counters and ceilings recorded from the honest instrument at b7f5fc7 (PERF-4a); before this the file was `{}` and gated nothing.

render-web ceiling raised 24195 -> 40947 B. Owner-authorized. The package took explicit ownership of the WebGL context (GetWebGLContext/MakeWebGLContext/MakeOnScreenGLSurface + paired teardown), gained webglcontextlost/restored self-healing, and its CanvasKit loader gained stall-abort, deadline and retry-after-failure. Added behaviour, not a regression. Note for future triage: source maps are ~61% of this package's gzipped dist (23254 B of 38242 B, summing per-file gzip of index.js.map, index.mjs.map, index.d.ts.map, index.d.mts.map against the full dist/), so byte growth here tracks source-map growth more than code growth.

New package @flare-engine/dynamics: ceiling CREATED at 37650 B (measured 34227 B, the standard 10% headroom). Creating a missing ceiling is the safe direction --write is allowed to take; no existing ceiling was raised (the run reported 1 created, 0 tightened, 41 left alone). The same `--write --bytes` run also refreshed `measured`/`measuredAt` fleet-wide to current reality — most are unchanged, audio fell 13565 -> 13522 B (a dead private field was removed) and core rose 20675 -> 21319 B with no source change in that package, which is pack-metadata drift rather than code growth. Counter scenarios were rewritten with identical values (no diff). Known-red at this commit and NOT addressed here: check:perf-freshness, which reports the published benchmark numbers as stale because commit 6a10aa9 (Vec2.perp/crossSV) changed sources that the ECS, Physics, Particles, Render and Integration suites transitively measure. Clearing it needs an owner-run recapture from a clean, quiet tree (bun run bench x5, bench:promote, bench:md) — an agent-run capture on a loaded machine would publish contended numbers, which is the failure mode PERF-1/PERF-5 exist to prevent.

ecs ceiling 24162 -> 32557 B and physics 22179 -> 36461 B. Owner-authorized, both from Arc CW7 (consumer-needs fixes, shipped in 0.3.1). ecs (+34.8% measured, 21965 -> 29597) is CW7-3: an optional caller-supplied `query?` on createLifetimeSystem/createBoundsCullSystem plus the JSDoc explaining when to pass one; the query is resolved once at construction and the per-frame closure is unchanged, confirmed by re-capture (ecs.step 1000 reads 9.40-9.95 us against 9.25-9.42 before). physics (+62.4% measured, 20409 -> 33146) is CW7-8's uniform spatial hash replacing the brute-force scan, plus CW7-6's collider readback pair. A hash is simply more code than a linear scan: item->slot Map, cell buckets, a packed bijective cell key that survives negative and far-from-origin coordinates, and stamp-based zero-alloc duplicate suppression. What the bytes bought, measured end-to-end on the published benchmark: physics.step 1000 AABB sparse 4.82 ms -> 172 us (28x), dense 5.38 ms -> 567 us (9.5x), and integration.frame 2000 entities 20.69 ms -> 1.10 ms (19x) — a real game frame moved from over-budget at 60 fps to comfortably inside it. Public surface frozen in both packages (ecs gained one optional parameter; the SpatialIndex exported surface diffed byte-identical against HEAD), so both shipped as patch. Added behaviour and a large measured speedup, not a regression.

Nine ceilings raised to measured x1.1, owner-authorized 2026-10-09 (pre-freeze audit). check:perf-bytes had been red since the September feature rows landed and nobody saw it, because it runs in neither verify.sh nor the release script — only in release.yml. Packed 0.3.1 -> now, with the commits that grew them: particles 13524 -> 22821 (OSS-M8 emitter shapes + drawParticles, ddd8116/2740004); errors 9658 -> 15386 (OSS-M7 global capture, 15424ba); core 21319 -> 33630 (PF-2b coroutine end states, fb5a0c5 — JSDoc-heavy); physics 33146 -> 50884 (OSS-M11 MTV + raycast, PF-6 addCollider/typed SolidGrid, HYG13 clamp, plus the 2026-10-09 boundary fix); ecs 29597 -> 38894 (PF-2a contracts, XR-7 swap-remove); math 61261 -> 77049 (OSS-M9 curves + RNG state, PF-2b); input 44353 -> 51805 (PF-3, OSS-B23b, HYG5-PRE docs); render 118178 -> 130368 (OSS-M10, PF-5); create 30570 -> 32794 (topdown door template, 5ce6021; renamed from create-flare-app, ADR-0007). Toolchain ruled out: every package whose source did not change measured exactly 0.0% different. Why a 95-line source diff costs core 12 KB: each source line ships up to six times — CJS and ESM output, two .d.ts files, and two source maps carrying sourcesContent — so JSDoc-heavy contract work is the expensive kind. Dropping sourcesContent from the published maps is the lever if these ceilings are ever to come back down; that is post-flip work, not a freeze change. Added behaviour, not a regression.

progression ceiling raised 17837 -> 38613 B (measured 35103 x1.1), authorized by the owner's approval of the PR closing issue #202 (rebuilt from the runner's #254 after a merge of main corrupted this file). New game-clock.ts exports createGameClock plus the GameClock, GameClockConfig, GameClockSegment and GameClockState types: a 1440-minute game-day clock with a validated per-segment real-seconds-per-game-hour table, boundary stepping that lands float-exactly on each boundary (advanceMinutes / skipTo compare an absolute target with each boundary; update carries real seconds and crosses when rounding lands on one), a skipTo that enters a start a released hold left the clock on, a pause() from a callback that stops the update in progress, an advance from a callback that cannot move it backwards, a restored state validated (paused a boolean, absoluteMinutes within Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER), a Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER bound on update and advanceMinutes, pause, hold at the next phase boundary, segment and phase change callbacks and a plain serialize state. Measured against the published 0.4.10 tarball, which equals main for this package (16211 B). So this change adds 18892 B gzipped (each file gzipped alone +14792 B): +6868 / +6842 B raw (+1999 / +1991 B gzipped) in dist/index.js / index.mjs, +15029 B raw (+4154 / +4158 B gzipped) in each source map, +2846 B raw (+984 B gzipped) in each .d.ts (JSDoc) and +737 B of README for the clock snippet. The package was small, so one module of ~250 lines doubles it; nothing else in the package moved. Added behaviour, not a regression.

No .d.ts change: both new modules are internal. A performance fix, not a regression.
